title: Only 57 of 2,248 mouse connections support held-out additive cell-delay tests in matched Allen slice graphs
abstract: We tested whether source-cell and target-cell terms predict omitted synaptic delays in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 slice data. A bipartite graph cycle is required for a unique omitted-edge prediction. Only 57 of 2,248 selected mouse VisP connections and four of 309 human TCx connections meet this condition within recording, synapse sign and ordered cell-class groups. These edges give 18 mouse and one human independent cycle constraints. On the mouse edges, the unregularized cell model had MSE 0.25617 ms squared, compared with 0.07273 for a group mean. Mean-minus-model MSE was -0.18344, with a nominal 95% inferred-donor bootstrap interval of -0.43501 to -0.05052. Strict label matching gave the same direction. Human support came from one inferred donor and does not support a population interval. Sparse graphs, measurement error, selected slices and inferred donors limit the result. The test does not rule out cell-specific timing or benefits from regularized models. We provide graph audits, code, predictions and reproducible evidence.

display.caption: Only connections on cycles support omitted-edge predictions under an additive source-plus-target model. Negative error gain favors the group mean. Human data have one donor and no interval.
